long_biography.plain_text:
Retail instincts appeared early for Mustafa Taviloğlu, who sold small goods from a bag while studying in Istanbul. In 1964, he and Doğan Gürün turned that experience into Mudo, opening a 12-square-metre shop in Beyoğlu's Fitaş Passage. Their first names supplied the brand name; Gürün later departed, leaving Taviloğlu to build the business.

Taviloğlu moved Mudo beyond gifts and records into printed T-shirts, fashion and home decoration, helping shape modern Turkish specialty retail. A parallel commitment began in 1972, when he acquired a painting by Necdet Kalay. Over the following decades, that purchase grew into the Taviloğlu Collection, which he eventually presented in full across seven Istanbul venues rather than limiting the public exhibition to selected works.
